name: the_WOW!_signal

phase_0.boundary_condition: The 72-second drift-scan window of the Big Ear telescope on 15 August 1977, bounded by Earth's rotation and the fixed beam pattern, enclosing the single detection event and all subsequent inference

⊢.justification: The state before the telescope beam intersects the signal — no detection, no candidate, no hypothesis

⊣.justification: The 72-second drift-scan window closes the system; after it passes, the source leaves the beam and no further data can be acquired

≻.justification: Forward morphism: the telescope receives and digitizes incoming radio power, transforming sky intensity into a recorded time-series

≺.justification: Reverse morphism: when a candidate hypothesis is falsified, the inference descends back to the undecided state while preserving open frames

⋈.justification: Composition: each processing stage (filtering, detection, characterization, follow-up) chains sequentially on the data product

⊙.justification: The recorded intensity profile (6EQUJ5) is its own identifier — the pattern recognizes itself across analyses

∈.justification: The single detection forks into three live arms: natural astrophysical, terrestrial interference, extraterrestrial artificial — each must be evaluated

∋.justification: The three hypothesis arms rejoin into a single classification record; conflicting evidence fuses to B (both plausible and implausible simultaneously)

⊤.justification: Deposits T: a positive match (e.g., narrowband width < 10 kHz, Doppler drift consistent with planetary rotation)

⊥.justification: Deposits F: a falsifying observation (e.g., no repetition in 100+ hours of follow-up, known satellite at that frequency)

⊞.justification: Holds B: the signal remains simultaneously a compelling SETI candidate and a probable statistical fluke — neither arm resolves

⊡.justification: The 6EQUJ5 printout and database entry are append-only; no later analysis can erase the original detection record

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No observation recorded; telescope idle or pointed elsewhere
phase_3.true_description: A hypothesis affirmed by constructive evidence (e.g., interference source identified and matched)
phase_3.false_description: A hypothesis refuted by constructive evidence (e.g., natural mechanism proven impossible at that bandwidth)
phase_3.both_description: The WOW! signal itself — simultaneously a genuine narrowband cosmic emission and an unexplained singleton; the paradigmatic B-state in SETI

steps.domain_action: Initialize the observation void — telescope powered, beam fixed, no target in field
Signal acquisition begins — Earth rotation sweeps beam across Sagittarius, receiver integrates 10-second samples
First pipeline stage — raw voltage samples composed into power spectra
Second pipeline stage — spectra composed into 50-channel intensity time-series
Third pipeline stage — time-series composed into alphanumeric intensity codes (0-9, A-Z)
The 6EQUJ5 pattern self-identifies — peak channel 'U' (30σ) recognizes its own structure
Affirmative evidence deposited — narrowband width < 10 kHz matches SETI search criteria (T-arm anchor)
Origin hypothesis fork opens — three arms activated: natural, interference, artificial
Natural arm sub-fork — maser vs flare vs comet sub-hypotheses
Maser sub-arm forward — evaluate astrophysical maser models at 1420 MHz
Maser sub-arm negative — no known maser produces 72-second drift-scan profile without repetition (F deposited)
Flare sub-arm forward — evaluate stellar flare hydrogen emission models
Flare sub-arm negative — flare duration and profile inconsistent with 72-second Gaussian shape (F deposited)
Comet sub-arm forward — evaluate comet hydrogen cloud models
Comet sub-arm negative — no known comet at those coordinates in 1977, velocity mismatch (F deposited)
Natural sub-fork rejoin — all sub-arms F, natural arm registers F
Natural arm reversal — hypothesis retracted, register cleared, frame preserved
Interference arm sub-fork — satellite vs aircraft vs ground transmitter sub-hypotheses
Satellite sub-arm forward — query 1977 satellite catalogs at 1420.456 MHz
Satellite sub-arm negative — no cataloged satellite at that frequency and drift rate (F deposited)
Aircraft sub-arm forward — evaluate aircraft transmitter harmonics near hydrogen line
Aircraft sub-arm negative — no flight paths match drift-scan geometry, bandwidth mismatch (F deposited)
Ground sub-arm forward — evaluate terrestrial interference, harmonics, intermodulation
Ground sub-arm negative — observatory in radio quiet zone, no local source matches profile (F deposited)
Interference sub-fork rejoin — all sub-arms F, interference arm registers F
Interference arm reversal — hypothesis retracted, register cleared, frame preserved
Artificial arm sub-fork — beacon vs leakage vs artifact sub-hypotheses
Beacon sub-arm forward — evaluate extraterrestrial beacon hypothesis, Doppler drift consistency
Beacon sub-arm affirmative — drift rate matches planetary rotation, frequency near hydrogen line (T deposited)
Leakage sub-arm forward — evaluate extraterrestrial radio leakage, planetary radar
Leakage sub-arm negative — power requirement exceeds plausible planetary leakage by orders of magnitude (F deposited)
Artifact sub-arm forward — evaluate instrumental artifact, data processing glitch
Artifact sub-arm negative — pattern persists across independent processing, not in calibration data (F deposited)
Paradice engaged — beacon sub-arm holds both T and F simultaneously (B-state)
Artificial sub-fork rejoin — beacon=B, leakage=F, artifact=F → artificial arm registers B
Classification rejoin — three arms fuse; natural=F, interference=F, artificial=B → register becomes B
Permanent log entry fixed — 6EQUJ5 recorded in observatory log, published, entered in SETI databases
Follow-up observation chain — subsequent epochs composed as null-result sequences
Green Bank 1997 follow-up — 14-hour observation at same coordinates, null result composed
Arecibo 2003 follow-up — high-sensitivity targeted search, null result composed
VLA 2012 follow-up — interferometric imaging of field, null result composed
META follow-up — all null results composed into meta-analysis, upper limits derived
Each follow-up deposits F — no repeat detection at same coordinates/frequency
Null results self-identify — each empty observation confirms its own emptiness
Observation window closure — the original 72-second window is the terminal anchor; no new data can enter
Final classification fixed — 'unresolved candidate' status permanently recorded in literature

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Big Ear data reduction pipeline (FORTRAN on IBM 1130) translating analog voltages into 50-channel alphanumeric printouts
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Shared magnetic tape and line-printer output between telescope operator, data analyst (Ehman), and follow-up observers
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Magnetic tape reels (raw data), fanfold paper printouts (processed), human notebooks (annotations), published literature (canonical record)
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Earth rotation (sidereal day) gates the observation window; follow-up scheduled by human proposal cycles
phase_5.alfs_store: The 6EQUJ5 printout with Ehman's red-ink 'WOW!' annotation — the canonical bootstrap artifact for all subsequent analysis

phase_6.cycle_cost: One 72-second drift-scan integration (~10^4 J telescope operating energy) plus 47 years of follow-up telescope time and compute
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Quiet sky at 1420 MHz; no candidate in database at RA 19h17m, Dec -27°
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Single high-SNR entry in SETI candidate database; persistent B-state classification; no repetition
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The detection extracts ~1 bit (signal vs noise) from thermal background; the persistent ambiguity (B-state) prevents entropy collapse to a definite T or F, conserving the information-theoretic cost of the observation

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: The WOW! signal appeared as a single, isolated transmission event without repetition, forming a sparse, non-repeating node in the network of SETI observations with no sustained or structured connectivity to other signals.
⊢=𐑨: The signal was detected as a narrowband radio emission originating from a specific celestial coordinate, propagating through three-dimensional space and requiring spatial localization to define its source and trajectory.
⊞=𐑳: The event involved a single, transient source detected by one receiver without any reciprocal or multi-party exchange, creating a fundamentally one-sided observation with no matched counterpart.
⊡=𐑷: The signal was a singular, non-repeating event with no inherent structural invariants, meaning its classification as an anomaly can be continuously deformed to a trivial noise artifact without crossing a topological boundary.
⊙=𐑢: The signal was a singular, isolated anomaly with no evidence of scale-free correlations, diverging susceptibility, or sustained critical dynamics, placing it firmly in the normal, subcritical regime of radio astronomy background noise.
⊥=𐑓: The signal exhibited no intrinsic handedness or orientational asymmetry in its polarization or structure, and its single, transient detection offers no persistent memory of symmetry breaking.
≻=𐑩: The detection of the signal was a passive, non-destructive measurement event based on pattern matching against background noise, with no energy transduction, structural change, or irreversible binding occurring between the source and the observer.
≺=𐑿: The signal propagation defines a clear directional vector from a distant source (donor) to the terrestrial receiver (acceptor), establishing a signed, asymmetric interface with no reciprocity or self-complementarity.
⋈=𐑱: The signal was a single, non-repeating event indistinguishable from a statistical fluctuation in background noise, offering no reproducible pattern or coding structure to constrain its origin, resulting in near-zero mutual information and high false-positive probability.
⊤=𐑘: The signal was a transient, non-repeating emission that appeared and vanished without any persistent structural state to rearrange, implying no kinetic barrier to its cessation or recurrence beyond the absence of a driving source.
∈=𐑲: The signal was a single, isolated detection event confined to one receiver at one time, with no propagation of influence to other detectors, frequencies, or subsequent observations, limiting its correlation length to a single measurement event.
∋=𐑜: The signal required only a single receiver tuned to the correct frequency and sky position to be detected, with no simultaneous multi-site or multi-instrument coincidence required for the observation to occur.
